basis: Syndromic developmental disability; skeletal involvement includes scoliosis in 6/10 and contractures in 4/10; mitral regurgitation in 3/10 meets threshold.
Developmental delay and cardiac malformations define syndrome; strabismus in 30-79% and clinodactyly in 7/15 support eye and skeletal involvement.
Ossification directly affects external ear cartilage.
Degenerative white-matter disease; ovarian insufficiency in 2/2 supports endocrine involvement; cataract in 1/1 supports ocular involvement, with limited sample size.
Type C dystroglycanopathies primarily cause skeletal muscle degeneration; cardiac and CNS involvement are not established in most patients across subtypes.
Brain malformations and developmental disability define the syndrome; hypospadias in 4/4 males is a urethral malformation. Other genital abnormalities are reproductive.
Malignancy of mast cells involving abdominal lymph nodes; mast cells are hematopoietic cells. This is not a lymphoma.
Primary breast adenocarcinoma with sebaceous differentiation; breast lies outside the axes, and sebaceous differentiation does not establish skin origin.
Isolated sperm motility and flagellar abnormalities causing male infertility; reproductive function lies outside the axes.
Epilepsy with both focal and generalized seizures is defined by cerebral dysfunction.
Direct injury or dysfunction of cranial nerves or their brainstem nuclei; resulting weakness does not establish intrinsic muscle or eye disease.
Liver cysts arise from bile duct epithelium. Although renal cysts occur in 14/25, the definition describes them as incidental without renal functional damage.
Tumour arises in the optic nerve sheath; the optic nerve belongs to the ocular axis. Intracranial extension is not required.
Benign peripheral nerve sheath tumour arising in the posterior mediastinum; location alone does not establish lung involvement.
Site-unspecified epithelial adenoma admixed with fat; the supplied morphology does not identify an organ, so no anatomical axis can be assigned reliably.
Conjunctival pterygia extending toward or onto the cornea; ancestry establishes an ocular lesion.
Lysosomal storage disorder with progressive neurodegeneration; retinal degeneration and visual loss occur in most patients with late infantile CLN8 disease.
Inherited enzyme deficiency causes hemolytic anemia; supplied phagocytic engulfment-defect ancestry supports immune dysfunction. Hyperbilirubinemia alone is not liver damage.
Peripheral axonal neuropathy, necrotizing encephalopathy and cerebral degeneration directly affect the nervous system.
Neurodegenerative PSP variant defined by progressive aphasia and speech apraxia; gaze abnormalities and motor findings arise from nervous system dysfunction.
Lymphoid malignancy directly occupies the retina; lymphoma warrants hematologic and immune axes. Associated CNS lymphoma is a separately diagnosed disease.
Congenital cerebral cortical malformation with cerebellar vermis hypoplasia.
Presynaptic neuromuscular junction disorder; weakness, ophthalmoparesis and apnea reflect impaired transmission rather than intrinsic muscle, eye or lung damage.
Congenital joint ankylosis and skeletal synostoses define disease; hearing impairment is annotated frequent (30-79%), supporting otologic involvement.
Inherited podocyte disease causing steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome. Secondary lipid changes and hypercoagulability do not establish additional organ damage.
